2. Implement a centralized logging configuration for the Spring-based application. This will enable easier monitoring and analysis of log system errors. Create a new configuration file `application.log.properties` in the root of the classpath with the following content:

logging.level.com.example.PatientRepository=INFO

3. Introduce a custom logging filter to suppress unnecessary log messages from being written to the console or file system. Create a new Java class `LogFilter` that extends `java.util.logging.Filter`:

public class LogFilter implements java.util.logging.Filter {
    @Override
    public boolean isLoggable(java.util.logging.LogRecord record) {
        return record.getLevel().intValue() >= java.util.logging.Level.INFO.intValue();
    }
}
```

```
java.util.logging.filter=LogFilter

This will ensure that only log messages with a level of INFO or higher are written to the console or file system.
